security_spec.violation_condition: In arch/riscv/kvm/vcpu_exit.c:kvm_riscv_vcpu_trap_redirect(), the guest VSTVEC CSR is read via ncsr_read(CSR_VSTVEC) and written directly to guest SEPC as the trap injection target without masking the low 2 MODE bits. If the guest has configured stvec.MODE=Vectored (MODE=1), the SEPC receives a misaligned address (BASE | 0x01). Since the injected traps are always synchronous exceptions, the spec requires using only the BASE address regardless of MODE, making this a direct spec violation that causes the guest to take an instruction-address-misaligned fault instead of the intended injected trap.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: ncsr_read(CSR_VSTVEC) used as sep= target without & ~0x3 mask
security_spec.summary: KVM trap redirection writes raw VSTVEC (including MODE bits) to guest SEPC, crashing guests that use Vectored stvec mode on trap injection

findings.finding: ncsr_read(CSR_VSTVEC) reads the raw vstvec CSR value including the low 2 MODE bits, and assigns it directly to guest_context.sepc as the trap injection target. When the guest has configured vstvec.MODE=Vectored (MODE=1), sepc receives BASE|0x01 — a misaligned address. Per the RISC-V spec, all synchronous exceptions (which is what trap_redirect injects) must use only the BASE field regardless of MODE. The injected trap causes an instruction-address-misaligned fault instead of the intended handler, resulting in guest DoS.

spec_citations.excerpt: The BASE field in stvec is a field that can hold any valid virtual or physical address, subject to the following alignment constraints: the address must be 4-byte aligned... When MODE=Direct, all traps into supervisor mode cause the pc to be set to the address in the BASE field. When MODE=Vectored, all synchronous exceptions into supervisor mode cause the pc to be set to the address in the BASE field, whereas interrupts cause the pc to be set to the address in the BASE field plus four times the interrupt cause number.

The vstvec register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that is VS-mode's version of supervisor register stvec, formatted as shown in Figure 73. When V=1, vstvec substitutes for the usual stvec, so instructions that normally read or modify stvec actually access vstvec instead.
